setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Keith played solo bass notes on piano near the closing refrain in a classic display; The reviewer remembers the song as having a great Jerry voice with conviction [11][16]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): The reviewer felt they almost lost it at the end of this song due to its quality; The reviewer considers this performance possibly the best they have heard from 1977 [8][13]
- **Mississippi Half-Step** (1 review): The performance is noted as one of the best ten, with a long, trippy loop [7]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): The reviewer specifically enjoyed hearing Jerry jam in this performance [9]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Jerry missed the cue to end the solo, leading the band to play the chorus [6]
- **Got My Mojo Workin'** (1 review): The performance is noted as a nice rare treat for the audience [14]

## The recordings

- **gd77-04-22.sbd.miller.27747.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 178 min; rated 4.2/5 by 30 [1]
- **gd1977-04-22.152296.aud.petrunis.andrewf.flac1644**: audience recording; 18 songs; 154 min [2]. Said about its sound: The recording sounds terrible due to low-fidelity gear and janky building acoustics [2]
- **gd77-04-22.sbd.cotsman.10148.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 148 min; rated 3.83/5 by 12 [3]
- **gd77-04-22.sony.unknown.8673.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 142 min; rated 2.88/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is described as hissy, cut in songs, and generally pathetic [5]

## Around the show

- The second set featured blown lyrics and strange lapses, contrasting with the first set's groove [6]
- The crowd is described as really into it, particularly during the Terrapin close [7]
- The audience was wild, screaming, and sang along to fill a gap in the Half-Step lyrics [8]
- The Philadelphia audience chanted along during the Half-Step in the old house with fine acoustics [11]
- Heads repeated the Mojo jam in the lot after the show, indicating strong audience engagement [16]
- The sound is compared favorably to the April 30, 1977 show, described as five skull material [13]
- This show is the first concert of what is called the best East Coast tour [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-04-22.sbd.miller.27747.sbeok.flacf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The recording is attributed to Betty Cantor-Jackson, whose boards are praised as the best; Transferred by Charlie Miller from Sony D8 DAT to RME Hammerfall Digiface and Sony Vaio [1][14]
- **gd1977-04-22.152296.aud.petrunis.andrewf.flac1644**: taped by Recording by Rich Petrunis.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 04/2021; source: Mono Sony hand-held recorder (model unknown) > Maxell-UD Set 1 & TDK-SD Set 2 (normal bias). [2]
- **gd77-04-22.sbd.cotsman.10148.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience [3]. Also: Seeded to etree by J. Cotsman, with sources including AUD, MC, D, and CD [3]
- **gd77-04-22.sony.unknown.8673.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM 99A mics [4]
